sections.label: Credit and non-credit co-ops
sections.summary: Singapore has 85 co-ops, including 24 credit co-ops with 140,000 members holding $820 million in deposits and $209 million in loans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: At present, there are 85 credit and non-credit co-ops in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Credit co-ops provide thrift and loan services to its members, who typically come from the same workplace, industry or community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: There are 24 credit co-ops serving 140,000 members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: As at 31 December 2016, members' deposits in credit co-ops amounted to $820 million, and loans to members amounted to $209 million.

sections.label: Co-operative Societies Act amendment
sections.summary: The Co-operative Societies Act was last amended in 2008 to enhance co-ops' governance and accountability amid growing membership and complex environments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Co-operative Societies Act was last amended in 2008 to enhance the governance and accountability of co-ops in view of their increasing membership and more complex operating environments.

sections.label: Registrar powers over credit co-ops
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Registrar cap dividends and stop errant credit co-ops from receiving new deposits if they fail prudential requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Bill enables the Registrar to impose a cap on such a co-op's dividends to members to ensure that most of its net surplus goes towards building up its institutional capital and strengthening its financial position.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: However, if a credit co-op persistently fails to meet any of the prudential requirements, the credit co-op would be putting members' deposits at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Hence, the Bill also empowers the Registrar to stop such errant credit co-ops from receiving any new deposits for such period as may be determined.

sections.label: Applicant number reduced to five
sections.summary: The Bill reduces the number of applicants required under the Act from at least 10 to five.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Act currently requires at least 10 applicants; the Bill reduces this number to five.

sections.label: New Permanent Shares class
sections.summary: The Bill expands co-ops' sources of capital by introducing a new class of Permanent Shares.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Bill expands co-ops' sources of capital by introducing a new class of "Permanent Shares".

sections.label: Documents before AGM
sections.summary: The Bill requires Audited Financial Statements and an Annual Report in a prescribed format to be made available to members before the AGM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: In order to ensure that members are adequately informed of the co-op's affairs, the Bill specifies that the documents that must be made available to members prior to the AGM include the Audited Financial Statements and the Annual Report.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Further to this, the Bill also stipulates that the Annual Report must be prepared in such format as may be prescribed by the Registrar to ensure adequate disclosure and transparency to its members.

sections.label: Strengthening credit co-op oversight
sections.summary: The passage states aims to strengthen regulatory oversight of credit co-ops and enhance powers to protect members' interests in distressed or errant co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: On the one hand, we seek to strengthen our regulatory oversight of credit co-ops in view of their fiduciary duty over members' deposits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: We also seek to enhance regulatory powers to enable us to better protect members' interests, especially in the case of distressed or errant co-ops.

sections.label: Welcoming credit co-op amendments
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes proposed legislative amendments that protect members' interests by raising governance standards, facilitating operations and enhancing regulatory powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Overall, I welcome the proposed legislative amendments that will further protect members' interests through raising governance standards of credit co-ops, facilitating their operations and enhancing regulatory powers.

sections.label: Registrar's power to wind up
sections.summary: Section 83 amendments empower the Registrar to order winding up of a co-op that breached terms and conditions of registration under section 9A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, the amendments in section 83 empower the Registrar to issue an order to wind up a cooperative if the Registrar is satisfied that the co-op has breached any of its terms and conditions of registration, varied or added under section 9A.

sections.label: Dividends from accumulated surplus
sections.summary: The passage states surpluses from previous financial years cannot be used for distribution and suggests allowing dividends from accumulated net surplus when no surplus exists that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Surpluses from other previous financial years, whether it is from accumulated surplus, retained earnings or their equivalent, cannot be used for distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I believe it would be useful for the Ministry to consider allowing a cooperative to pay dividends out of its accumulated net surplus if there is no surplus for that year in which the dividend is declared.

sections.label: Drawdown from reserves for dividends
sections.summary: The speaker notes the Acts do not specify dividends from accumulated surplus, cites co-op figures, and hopes the Ministry permits drawdown from reserves for dividends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I note that both the Companies Act and the Co-operative Societies Act of 2009 do not specify whether dividends can be declared from accumulated surplus even if there is no surplus for the current year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I have also asked the Singapore National Co-operative Federation and they have told me that based on the recent three years' audited accounts, there were nine loss-making co-ops with positive reserves, that is, their dividends could have been drawn down from reserves and that there were 20 profitable co-ops that declared dividends of lower than 10%, which is the maximum allowable under the Co-operative Societies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All boards have fiduciary duties to perform and I think we should not be overly prescriptive in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Where they have reasons to make such a recommendation, the members of the co-op also have a say in approving or rejecting such a recommendation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Where there are grounds for the Registrar of Societies to act against the cooperative or its board, I believe, with the proposed changes, the Registrar is empowered to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All things considered and for reasons stated above, I hope the Ministry can consider permitting drawdown from reserves for dividend payments and to incorporate this change in this amendment Bill.

sections.label: Embezzlement at co-op society
sections.summary: The passage states a recent case involved embezzlement of $1.5 million at the Singapore Statutory Boards Employee's Co-operative Thrift and Loan Society, calling it a wake-up call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The recent case pertaining to the embezzlement of funds totalling $1.5 million at the Singapore Statutory Boards Employee's Co-operative Thrift and Loan Society is wake-up call for all of us.

sections.label: Credit co-op deposits and assets
sections.summary: There are 23 active credit co-operatives with assets totalling nearly $1 billion serving 138,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What is more of a concern is the huge amount of money that is deposited with our credit co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There are 23 such active co-operatives, with assets totalling nearly $1 billion serving 138,000 members.

sections.label: NTUC Thrift closure 2013
sections.summary: NTUC Thrift and Loan, with 29,000 members and over $17 million in deposits, closed after struggling to offer competitive returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Will they compared against banks, which also offer loans and take in deposits?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I ask these questions because if we throw back our minds to 2013, the largest credit co-op of the time, NTUC Thrift and Loan, which was well managed and I was a member of, with 29,000 members and over $17 million in deposits, decided to close their operations because they had struggled for years to offer their co-op members competitive returns in a low interest environment that continues to prevail today.

sections.label: Safeguards for credit co-operatives
sections.summary: The Ministry is putting in place safeguards to protect members' interests in credit co-operatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But these days, the landscape has changed and, therefore, harder measures are required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am therefore pleased that the Ministry is putting in place safeguards to protect members' interests in credit co-operatives.

sections.label: Co-op employees defrauded savings
sections.summary: Two employees of a co-op abused their trust over five years, defrauding it of more than $5 million of members' savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In a recently publicised case, two employees of one of Singapore's oldest co-ops had systematically abused their position of trust over a period of five years by reaching into the co-op's coffers to feed their extravagant lifestyle, defrauding the co-op of more than $5 million of the members' savings.

sections.label: Training for key committee members
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry to elaborate on mandatory training and qualification requirements for key committee members managing large sums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry elaborate more on the requisite training and qualification requirements that will be made mandatory for key committee members or those who will manage the large sums of money, particularly in a credit co-op?

sections.label: Lowering minimum qualification age
sections.summary: Section 60 of the Bill lowers the minimum qualification age for the Committee of Management from 21 to 18 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As such, I feel that section 60 of the Bill, which seeks to lower the minimum qualification age for the Committee of Management from 21 to 18 years old, appears to run contrary to the intent of the Bill to tighten corporate governance and improve competencies.

sections.label: Annual ranking of credit co-ops
sections.summary: A request for the Ministry to consider introducing an annual ranking or grading of credit co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the point about tightening governance, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider introducing an annual ranking of sorts or grading of the credit co-ops.

sections.label: Credit co-op membership and deposits
sections.summary: As of November 2017, 24 active credit co-ops serve about 138,000 members with $820 million deposited and almost $209 million loaned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of November 2017, there are 24 active credit co-ops serving approximately 138,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Members have deposited approximately $820 million in these co-ops and these entities have loaned out almost $209 million to their members.

sections.label: Clause 55 co-op officer training
sections.summary: Clause 55 lets the Minister make rules on qualifications and training of co-op officers, which the speaker calls a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Good governance requires both a robust regulatory framework as well as officers who are well-versed in corporate governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that clause 55 in the Bill that allows the Minister to make rules for or with respect to the qualifications and training requirements of co-op officers is thus a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Clause 54 Registrar removal powers
sections.summary: Clause 54 empowers the Registrar to remove a co-op's committee of management and appoint individuals to take over when it is mismanaged or has misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 54 empowers the Registrar to protect the co-op by vesting the Registrar with the authority to remove the committee of management of the society and appoint one or more individuals to take over the management and administration of the co-op when the co-op is mismanaged or when there are instances of misconduct.

sections.label: Clauses 6, 24, 30 inclusivity
sections.summary: Clauses 6, 24 and 30 clarify ordinary and management committee membership and reduce the minimum number to set up a co-op to five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clauses 6, 24, and 30 of the amended Bill aims to promote inclusivity by clarifying who can be an ordinary member and a management committee member of co-ops and reduces the minimum number of people to set up a co-op to five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that these changes will collectively facilitate the setting up of co-ops, encourage more groups to promote their goals, and will contribute to the development of a stronger civic society in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, while some co-ops do function as business entities, they also have a strong social mission to help Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is important that we continue to support the growth and development of these entities by creating a facilitative climate that both reduces the barriers to set up co-ops, as well as instil a stronger operating framework to safeguard members' interests.

sections.label: Extended powers and deposit insurance
sections.summary: The speaker questions the need for extended powers, notes 85 co-ops with $8.76 billion in assets, and suggests deposit insurance for credit co-op deposits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I wonder if these extended powers are necessary, and hope the Minister can provide clarifications on why this is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have 85 co-ops currently, of which 24 are credit co-ops, with assets totalling $8.76 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These are not small sums of money and a recent incident of fraud at one of our co-ops highlights the need for more vigilance and stringent controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For credit co-ops, I would like to suggest that the members' deposits be covered by deposit insurance, similar to the deposits with our financial institutions.

sections.label: Credit co-ops and supervision
sections.summary: Credit co-ops should face supervisory frameworks similar to those for finance companies regulated by MAS, given their services and 140,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Credit co-ops should also be subject to relevant and similar supervisory frameworks which now apply to finance companies regulated by MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: They play important social and economic functions for their members, offering a range of services from supermarket to welfare and financial services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We know that there are now about 23 credit co-operatives that offer a range of financial services, such as loans and fixed deposits, and encourage their 140,000 members to save for a rainy day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Many co-op members are also long-time members and some even have their family members as associate members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It was therefore disappointing to read about the case involving employees from the Singapore Statutory Boards Employees' Co-op cheating the society of more than $5 million, as also pointed out by Mr Alex Yam.

sections.label: Co-ops meeting financial obligations
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether any co-operative in the last five years was unable to meet financial obligations and protect members' interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In that regard, I would like to ask, for the last five years, has any co-operative been in jeopardy and was unable to meet its financial obligations and protect members' interests?

sections.label: Loans written off by co-ops
sections.summary: The speaker asks what percentage of loans credit co-ops wrote off and whether this is comparable with other financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What percentage of loans had to be written off by credit co-ops and is this comparable with other financial institutions?

sections.label: Bill strengthens credit co-op oversight
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments largely focus on strengthening regulatory oversight of credit co-ops that take deposits and grant loans to members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In this Bill, the amendments largely focus on strengthening our regulatory oversight of credit co-ops as they take in deposits and grant loans to members.

sections.label: Registrar winding up a co-op
sections.summary: Under new regulations, the Registrar will not wind up a co-op unless insolvent, failing minimum requirements, or acting against national security or members' interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In addition, under the new regulations, the Registrar will not wind up a co-op unless the co-op is insolvent, wilfully fails to meet the minimum prescribed requirements or if its operations run contrary to national security or the members' interests.

sections.label: Co-ops disclosing terms to members
sections.summary: To increase transparency, co-ops will be required to disclose information on new or modified terms and conditions to their members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We agree with Mr Ng that for greater transparency, a co-op should disclose pertinent information to its members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Hence, we will require the co-op to disclose information on any new or modified terms and conditions to their members.

sections.label: Co-op and Registrar appointments
sections.summary: A co-op and the Registrar may appoint up to two temporary new members without veto power until the next AGM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, we recognise there is a need for additional injection of competencies and diversity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Hence, we provide the flexibility for a co-op and the Registrar to appoint up to two new members, with no veto power and on a temporary basis, to serve until the next AGM.

sections.label: Minimum competency standards for officers
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation will set minimum competency standards, covering work experience and qualifications, for selected key officers including Audit Committee members, CEO and CFO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The minimum competency standards we will introduce through subsidiary legislation, which comprise the number of years of relevant work experience as well as minimum qualifications, will be applicable to selected key officers, such as a member of the Audit Committee, the CEO and the CFO.

sections.label: CCF subsidies and transition period
sections.summary: CCF subsidy schemes were revised to give credit co-ops more financial support for training, and existing officers get a three-year transition period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, subsidy schemes under CCF have been revised to provide more financial support to the credit co-ops to undergo training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A transition period of three years is also granted to existing officers to meet the new requirements.

sections.label: Deposit Insurance Scheme coverage
sections.summary: The Deposit Insurance Scheme cannot cover credit co-ops because they are not part of the banking system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Deposit Insurance Scheme (DIS) is unable to cover credit co-ops as they are not part of the banking system.

sections.label: External audit of financial statements
sections.summary: All credit co-ops' financial statements will be externally audited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: All credit co-ops' financial statements will be externally audited.

sections.label: Bad loans written off 2016
sections.summary: Bad loans written off by credit co-ops in Financial Year 2016 was about $2.3 million, about 1% of total outstanding loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For loans granted by credit co-ops, the bad loans written off for Financial Year 2016 was about $2.3 million, which is about 1% of the total outstanding loans.

sections.label: Lowering minimum age for committee
sections.summary: Lowering the minimum age for a Committee of Management member from 21 to 18 primarily facilitates tertiary students' participation in university co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: On the lowering of the minimum age for a Committee of Management member from 21 to 18, I would like to clarify in response to Mr Melvin Yong that this is primarily to facilitate the participation of tertiary students in university co-ops, for example.

sections.label: Secret ballot requirement
sections.summary: The requirement of the secret ballot is to protect the interest of individual members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The requirement of the secret ballot is, in fact, to protect the interest of individual members.

sections.label: Relooking matter in next review
sections.summary: They are prepared to relook this matter as part of the next review of the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, we are prepared to relook this matter as part of the next review of the legislation.
